title: Sharp order-preserving integer models for short additive equalities
summary: We ask how small an increasing integer model of a finite real set can be while preserving all equalities between equal-length sums of at most $q$ elements, with repetitions allowed. The increasing correspondence must preserve exactly which sums are equal; the signs of unequal comparisons may change. Let $H_m(q)$ be the least diameter sufficient for every ordered real set of size $m$. For every integer $q\ge2$ we prove $H_4(q)=q(q+1)$ and $H_5(q)=q^2(q+1)$, and we determine $H_6(2)=24$.
